notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Smoother PSP and Dreamcast: these games stuttered because only about 44 to 47 of every 60 frames reached the screen. They now run on a screen path that shows every frame once, about 59 of 60, at the same game speed. The Frame pacing setting in each game's Performance settings is Automatic by default; Full speed brings the previous path back, and VSync keeps the lock even under the stats overlay.

Games that draw through Vulkan (PS1, GameCube, Wii, PS2, Wii U, 3DS, and ports such as Banjo-Kazooie and Donkey Kong 64) now hold the GPU at 845 MHz while they run. The GPU clock used to idle under a light scene and the game fell to half speed; a PSP scene that ran at 34 frames a second on the idle clock runs at 56. The floor is released when the game closes, and Battery Saver keeps its own lower ceiling. The GPU clock setting for Wii U games now says Auto (845 MHz).

The stats overlay is now drawn inside the game's picture instead of in a window over it, so SNES, N64, PSP, Dreamcast and the other smooth paths keep their frames with it on: about 58 of 60, up from 50. It also shows the game's frame rate and frame time. The pause menu's Performance overlay switch hides and shows it as before. DS and 3DS games, PC games and netplay keep the overlay window.

The SCCM Retro app no longer offers a Home menu icon on a console that runs from the system memory (sysMMC), where an installed icon can get the console banned from Nintendo's online services. On an emuMMC it is offered as before. When the app cannot tell which one the console runs from, it warns and asks for a three-second ZL + ZR hold before adding the icon. The new app ships with this update and is on the download page.

Not tried yet: docked play on the new PSP and Dreamcast path and with the overlay drawn in the picture; the overlay's horizontal bar sits at the top left whatever position is set. The app's Home menu change was tried in a preview, not on a console. GameCube, Wii, 3DS and PS1 still lose about one frame in six with tear-free on; their OpenGL paths measured worse, so they stay as they are.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
